'''Katharine A.''' "'''Katy'''" '''Ott''' is an American mathematician specializing in [[harmonic analysis]] and [[partial differential equation]]s, and known for her advocacy of [[women in mathematics]]. She is a professor of mathematics at [[Bates College]] in [[Lewiston, Maine]], where she chairs the Department of Mathematics.{{r|profile}}

==Education and career==
Ott is originally from [[Cumberland, Maine]].{{r|welcome}} She was an undergraduate at [[Middlebury College]], graduating in 2003. She went to the [[University of Virginia]] for graduate study in mathematics, received a master's degree there in 2005, and completed her Ph.D. in 2008.{{r|cv}} Her doctoral dissertation, ''Boundary Integral Equations in Non-Smooth Domains'', was supervised by [[Irina Mitrea]].{{r|mg}}

After postdoctoral research at the [[University of Kentucky]], she continued at the University of Kentucky as an assistant professor beginning in 2011.{{r|cv}} At the University of Kentucky, she organized the Sonia Kovalevsky Day program of activities for female secondary school students and their teachers.{{r|skd}} In 2014 she moved to Bates College;{{r|welcome}} she was tenured there as an associate professor in 2018 and promoted to full professor in 2024.{{r|cv}}

==Recognition==
For her work organizing the Sonia Kovalevsky Day program, Ott received the 2014 [[AWM Service Award|National Service Award]] of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]].{{r|skd}} She was named a Fellow of the Association for Women in Mathematics in 2024, "for immense dedication to outreach to girls and women, including directing GirlsGetMath at ICERM; supporting AWM through committees, grant-writing, the newsletter, and AWM’s USA Science and Engineering Festival booth; and leading award-winning tutoring and volunteering initiatives in Maine".{{r|fawm}}

Bates College gave Ott the 2023 Kroepsch Award for Excellence in Teaching, the highest teaching award of the college.{{r|kroepsch}}
